target: Whether to ship the first public release this week
direct_read: The release is possible, but the current plan is optimizing polish before testing demand.
observed_facts: The repository has a runnable local test suite.
No external user feedback has been collected yet.
assumptions: More README polish will materially improve adoption before a first user test.

blind_spots.claim: The launch page must be perfect before sharing it.
blind_spots.challenge: Perfection is being used as a gate without evidence that it reduces the main adoption risk.
blind_spots.consequence: Time is spent on presentation while the demand assumption remains untested.
blind_spots.test: Share the current version with five target users and record whether they install or ask a question.

opportunity_cost: Each week spent polishing instead of testing delays evidence about whether the problem matters.

priorities.change: Run a small user test before adding more polish.
priorities.why: It reduces the highest-impact uncertainty first.
priorities.next_action: Send the repository to five relevant users and ask them to install one workflow.
priorities.proof: Five responses are recorded with install attempts, blockers, and requested changes.

priorities.change: Fix only blockers found in the test.
priorities.why: It keeps effort tied to observed friction.
priorities.next_action: Group feedback into adoption, usability, and feature requests.
priorities.proof: Every change references a reported blocker or is explicitly deferred.

uncertainty: UNVERIFIED: whether the intended users will adopt the workflow after installation.
